quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Six times
20 times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: How does the stopping distance for motorcycles compare to cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, wet or slippery roads make it harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have been operating that motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a road with good traction, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear brake locks on a road with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop. You will still be able to steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip from car drippings. This strip:

options.text: Is never safe for motorcyclists.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided since other parts of the lane are drier.
Adds traction to most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area still provides enough traction for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When a group of motorcyclists enters a highway or curve, they should:

options.text: Ride single-file.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is usually best, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing up, what does it mean?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing up, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it smoothly.
Release the front brake and push harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply it smoothly again.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What is the proper footwear for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Shoes with long, loose laces.
Shoes with short heels.
Shoes with tall heels.
Always sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes with short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on rough surfaces. Keep laces tucked in so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: What should you do on a long motorcycle trip?

options.text: Skip rest breaks to save time.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel drowsy.
Wear warm clothing to protect from wind, cold, and rain.
Ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothing to protect from wind, cold, and rain.
questions.explanation: To stay fresh on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Limit riding to no more than 6 hours per day. Take rest breaks at least every 2 hours. Avoid stimulants—they only cause extreme tiredness when they wear off.

questions.question: Is it good to wear a riding jacket in hot weather?

options.text: Yes, it helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
No, it causes heat-related problems.
Only if the jacket is light colored.
No, it is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Always wear a riding jacket and long pants, even in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to other safety benefits.

questions.question: How long can marijuana effects last?

options.text: No more than 15 minutes.
About 1 hour.
About 2 hours.
More than 6 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than 6 hours.
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana begins to affect the user within minutes and effects last 2 to 4 hours. Eaten marijuana takes over 1 hour to begin working but effects can last more than 6 hours.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: The left side.
The center.
The right side.
It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: How should you turn your motorcycle?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Don't hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Don't lean the motorcycle because it's unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than walking speed, your motorcycle needs to lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn to lean the correct way.

questions.question: Helmeted riders are how many times more likely to survive a crash?

options.text: Two times.
Three times.
Eight times.
Ten times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times.
questions.explanation: At any speed, wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash than riding without a helmet.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are white with black lettering and tell you about road rules like speed limits. You must follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: What is NOT a benefit of proper riding clothes?

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a collision.
Protection from cold weather.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you in a crash and protect against wind, cold, and rain. They provide comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Just behind the leader.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should stay near the front, just behind the leader. This way they won't have to rush to keep up. More experienced riders behind them can also watch and help them.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they feel most comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride right behind the leader near the front. This lets experienced riders watch them from the back of the group.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Make angry gestures at other drivers.
Ride in a zigzag pattern across the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
The best position changes based on driving conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best position changes based on driving conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Choose a position based on your current conditions. Make sure you can stay visible and have enough space around you.

questions.question: What is true about the rounded mirrors on most motorcycles?

options.text: They are easy to adjust to immediately.
They make cars look closer than they are.
They show a narrow view behind you.
They make cars look farther away than they are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make cars look farther away than they are.
questions.explanation: Rounded mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, objects appear farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to rounded mirrors.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following except:

options.text: Help you see better and be seen by others.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Block your escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape routes.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen. It should keep you out of blind spots and help you avoid hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears. Your lane position should never block your escape routes.
